headline: Two functions package the changed files and neither build carries the change: irpt-ycharts-generate (uploads.py pinned at f09b802cdc, template_reader.py pinned at 3f29017cfc) and irpt-status (ops/status.py pinned at 361c44fa9d). The irpt-status build equals the live package byte for byte (6idtFvAmY...); the irpt-ycharts-generate build differs from live by four members that are not this round's (acceptance.py, durable_job.py, submission.py, submission_service.py). THE RELEASE IS WIDER THAN 'a sheet accepted yesterday is turned back': UploadService.read_input (uploads.py:614-637) re-reads the retained original with whichever template_reader is deployed and requires the result to EQUAL the template stored at acceptance, so after the release an input accepted yesterday whose bytes the new reader reads differently (a workbook with a second sheet, an account column with two values, a total row) is REFUSED on every re-open: the same token re-posted, the submit of a request on it, a refresh that supersedes it (measured in process: UploadRefused TEMPLATE_ORIGINAL_BINDING). The reader also runs in a second runtime, the resident, installed from its own tarball; with only the Lambda released, every multi-sheet workbook is accepted by the old resident and then refused by the new Lambda on the next poll (measured in process). The two runtimes must carry the same reader.

accepted_yesterday_turned_back_today.branch_turned_back: A synthetic csv 'Ticker,Dollars / AAA,100 / BBB,200 / Total,300' (made-up tickers). Yesterday, with every symbol answered FOUND (the offline stub of this cell; the live provider's answer for TOTAL was NOT read), the door accepted it as NORMALIZED. After the release the POST's FIRST answer is {upload_id: UP-<64 hex>, input_id: null, state: 'NEEDS_CORRECTION', reason: 'TEMPLATE_FINDINGS', findings: [{code: 'TOTAL_ROW_PRESENT', severity: 'ERROR', row: 4, column: 'A', value: 'Total', actions: ['REPLACE_FILE'], description: 'Row 4 is a total, not a holding. Remove the row and upload the file again; the report adds up your holdings itself.'}], findings_total: 1, template: <the full read>} (template_reader.py:292, uploads.py:465-473; measured in process: 0 messages sent to the resident). WRITTEN: the UPLOAD# row and the retained ORIGINAL_HOLDINGS object are written BEFORE the read (uploads.py:376-387 then :401), so a turned-back sheet still leaves an upload record and an original that cannot be deleted; NOT written: no NORMALIZATION# row, no INPUT# row, no NORMALIZED_PORTFOLIO object, no queue message. A PERSON SEES: PROD form (Ticket Center) 'Review required: TEMPLATE_FINDINGS Nothing was filed.' then the line 'Row 4: Row 4 is a total, not a holding. ...' (the form prefixes 'Row N: ' to words that already begin 'Row N', analysisRequest.ts:77-78); DEV form shows 'the file needs a correction' with the same line and the raw reason inside a closed Details; the Analysis card shows 'Review required: TEMPLATE_FINDINGS Row 4.' and the list (ProspectComposer.tsx:443-459). The same holds for a second account column (ACCOUNT_COLUMN_SEVERAL_VALUES, row 1, column letter, no account value in any finding) and a repeated header row (HEADER_ROW_REPEATED); a repeated header was already turned back for AMOUNT_NOT_A_NUMBER (measured), so it only gains a second line.
accepted_yesterday_turned_back_today.branch_still_accepted: The same sheet minus the offending row (AAA 100, BBB 200), or minus the extra account column: the POST answers {state: 'RESOLVING', input_id: null} exactly as yesterday (no findings, no reason, no template; uploads.py:474-480), the resident accepts it, the next POST answers NORMALIZED with a portfolio identical in shape to yesterday's (measured: read_input and the re-POST both OK for a clean csv and a one-sheet workbook; reader projection identical old vs new). What changes for an accepted workbook with a SECOND SHEET (even a sheet of junk): the accepted answer's portfolio.findings and portfolio.template.findings gain one NOTICE {code: 'SHEETS_NOT_READ', severity: 'NOTICE', value: '1', actions: ['REVIEW'], description: 'Only the first sheet was read; 1 other sheet(s) in this workbook were not. ...'} (measured). The state stays NORMALIZED. No portal reader shows it (rows above), so the person sees nothing new on an accepted sheet.
accepted_yesterday_turned_back_today.what_happens_to_inputs_already_accepted: YES, a stored input is re-read by the new reader, and an input accepted yesterday FAILS today where the new reader reads its original differently. uploads.py:614-637 read_input re-reads the retained ORIGINAL with read_template (:632-636) and refuses with UploadRefused('TEMPLATE_ORIGINAL_BINDING') unless the result EQUALS document['template'], the whole projection (findings included) stored at acceptance (portfolio.py:499). The Entry maps the refusal to an ok:false envelope with state UNAVAILABLE and public reason INVALID_INPUT (observed in the in-process Entry). Callers: (1) the re-POST of the same token (uploads.py:397-399 -> _answer :499 -> _normalized_response :599); (2) the submit of an analysis request on a held input (ycharts/generate/prospect_submission.py:68, and again :79); (3) a refresh that supersedes an input (uploads.py:362). Measured in process on synthetic sheets (accepted with the pinned-3f29017cfc reader, re-opened with HEAD's): clean csv OK/OK; one-sheet workbook OK/OK; two-sheet workbook REFUSED/REFUSED; csv with an Account column of two values REFUSED/REFUSED; csv with a Total row REFUSED/REFUSED (read_input / re-POST). So the pair MUST cover: every accepted multi-sheet workbook, every accepted two-account sheet and every accepted total-row sheet becomes unopenable and its pending requests unsubmittable the moment a runtime with the new reader serves them. The re-read is in the generate Lambda only (the resident never calls read_input). The pair needs one of: a step that counts how many accepted template inputs the new reader reads differently (counts only, no content; the enrichment list names this as item 6, a separate window), a change that makes read_input compare only what the old reader could have produced (outside this cell: a product edit), or an accepted loss of those inputs. Rows already in flight: a RESOLVING row at the release is resolved by whichever resident package is installed then; a stored NEEDS_CORRECTION row is re-answered with its stored findings and a template re-read today (:512,:516), so the two may disagree but nothing is refused. Request records already issued keep their input_ref and are not re-read by the reader (no read_input caller in the resident or the status path).
